course_name: AI-Integrated Video Editing & Motion Graphics Professional
target_audience: Aspiring video editors, motion graphic designers, digital content creators, marketing professionals, and creative freelancers seeking an end-to-end commercial post-production skillset. The program begins with foundational visual storytelling and requires no prior editing or animation experience, systematically advancing to professional junior and mid-level production readiness.

prerequisites.eligibility: Open to beginners. No prior professional editing, motion graphics, or programming experience required.
prerequisites.required_foundations: Comfort with desktop operating systems (file management, folder hierarchies, unzipping archives), visual curiosity, and commitment to 8-10 hours of weekly guided and independent production work.
prerequisites.recommended_background: Basic familiarity with digital photography, social video trends, or creative software (Canva, Photoshop, or basic video apps) is helpful but not mandatory.

system_requirements.operating_system: Windows 11 (64-bit) or macOS Sonoma / Ventura (Apple Silicon M1/M2/M3/M4 recommended).
system_requirements.processor: Intel Core i7/i9 (12th gen or newer), AMD Ryzen 7/9, or Apple Silicon M1 Pro/Max or better.
system_requirements.memory_ram: 16 GB RAM minimum; 32 GB RAM strongly recommended for comfortable After Effects and DaVinci Resolve caching.
system_requirements.graphics_gpu: Dedicated GPU with minimum 4 GB VRAM (NVIDIA RTX 3060 / 4060 or AMD Radeon equivalent; Apple Silicon unified memory).
system_requirements.storage: 512 GB SSD internal drive minimum, plus an external 1 TB or 2 TB USB-C SSD (Crucial X8/Samsung T7 or similar) dedicated to media caches and raw 4K video footage.
system_requirements.display: 1920x1080 resolution minimum; 100% sRGB color-accurate display recommended for color grading.

software_and_subscriptions.adobe_creative_cloud: Students require access to Adobe Premiere Pro, After Effects, Illustrator, Photoshop, and Media Encoder. Student educational pricing is available through Adobe.
software_and_subscriptions.davinci_resolve: Free DaVinci Resolve is fully sufficient for all classroom exercises and portfolio deliverables. Studio version is optional and clearly demarcated.
software_and_subscriptions.generative_ai_platforms: Free tiers and starter credits in Adobe Firefly, Google Flow, and Runway are utilized for classroom demonstrations. Students budget small nominal platform credits for independent generation as detailed in Module 20.

overview: Learn professional video editing, motion graphics, VFX compositing, cinematic colour grading, audio post-production and AI-powered video production using Premiere, After Effects, DaVinci Resolve, Adobe Firefly, Google Flow and Runway. Build client-style commercial projects and a professional showreel.

why_now.industry_shift: Video now constitutes over 82% of all global internet consumer traffic. Brands, advertising agencies, and tech companies are aggressively shifting budgets from static graphic design into dynamic motion systems and video campaigns.
why_now.the_hybrid_filmmaker_imperative: The emergence of generative AI video models has fundamentally transformed commercial post-production. Employers no longer hire editors who only know how to cut clips, nor do they hire 'prompt-only' novices whose raw AI clips contain distorted faces and boiling edges. The market rewards hybrid craftspeople who master cinematic editing, physics-based motion design, and color grading, using AI as an accelerator for visual extensions.
why_now.commercial_urgency: Production timelines have compressed from months to days. Studios actively seek video generalists who can handle the entire pipeline from storyboarding to motion templates and multi-platform social delivery without handing off to four different specialists.

learning_outcomes: Interpret commercial video briefs, client objectives, and target audience calls to action (CTA).
Edit professionally in Premiere Pro using high-retention 3-point cuts, trimming tools, and proxy workflows.
Build retention-oriented short-form vertical videos for social platforms (TikTok, Instagram Reels, YouTube Shorts).
Manage multi-camera and long-form footage pipelines with synchronized audio and organized bin taxonomy.
Create original After Effects motion graphics using vector shape layers, modifiers, and kinetic layout grids.
Animate brand identity systems including logo stings, broadcast titles, lower thirds, and intro/outro bumpers.
Use expressions (wiggle, loopOut, valueAtTime, linear) and Graph Editor speed curves for physics-based animation.
Track and composite footage using point tracking, planar tracking in Mocha AE, and the 3D Camera Tracker.
Perform practical rotoscoping and VFX subject isolation using Roto Brush 3.0, Refine Edge, and clean plates.
Grade video in DaVinci Resolve using node-based workflows, primary wheels, and Colour-Space Transforms (CST).
Clean and mix audio using Fairlight, applying dialogue cleanup, parametric EQ, compression, and loudness mastering.
Generate controlled AI video shots using Adobe Firefly, Google Flow, and Runway with prompt engineering.
Combine real and generated footage seamlessly on mixed-media timelines with matching lighting, grain, and blur.
Maintain visual and motion continuity across multi-scene narrative arcs and multi-camera perspectives.
Review copyright, synthetic-media permissions, biometric consent, and C2PA content provenance disclosures.
Deliver professional multi-format exports complying with broadcast MXF, Apple ProRes, and optimized web codecs.
Prepare client-ready project documentation including shot breakdowns, iteration budgets, and handoff archives.
Present a credible professional showreel with verified project evidence and defend technical choices in interviews.

faq.question: Can complete beginners without prior editing or animation experience enroll in this course?
faq.answer: Yes. The course begins with foundational visual storytelling, cinematic composition, and computer workspace setup in Month 1. You will be systematically guided through basic cutting and keyframing before advancing into complex procedural animation, visual effects, and color grading. No prior knowledge of Premiere Pro, After Effects, or video theory is required.

faq.question: What is the total duration and guided learning commitment for this program?
faq.answer: The program spans exactly 8 Months comprising 320 Guided Production Hours across 26 structured modules. Students should plan for 10 hours of structured guided instruction per week, plus an additional 6–8 hours of independent classroom lab drills, project editing, and creative practice.

faq.question: What specific editing skills and workflows are covered in Adobe Premiere Pro?
faq.answer: You will master Premiere Pro 26.5 from ingest to master delivery: workspace configuration, 3-point timeline editing, Ripple/Rolling/Slip/Slide trim tools, multicam sequence syncing, proxy workflows for 4K media, speech enhancement, text-based transcript editing, dynamic audio ducking, Essential Graphics panel title styling, and multi-format export presets.

faq.question: How deeply does the program cover Adobe After Effects and motion graphics?
faq.answer: After Effects receives 40 hours of dedicated foundation training in Months 3–4 plus ongoing integration in Months 5–8. You will master transform keyframing, anchor point alignment, the Graph Editor for custom speed curves, shape layer modifiers (Trim Paths, Repeaters), per-character kinetic text range selectors, track mattes, procedural JavaScript expressions (wiggle, loopOut, valueAtTime, linear), and packaging responsive Motion Graphics Templates (.mogrt) for Premiere Pro.

faq.question: How is DaVinci Resolve and Fairlight audio post-production integrated into the curriculum?
faq.answer: Month 6 dedicates 32 guided hours specifically to DaVinci Resolve: 20 hours of professional node-based color correction and grading (reading Waveforms, RGB Parades, Vectorscopes, Colour-Space Transforms from camera Log profiles, shot matching, and skin-tone correction) followed by 12 hours of audio post-production in Fairlight (dialogue cleanup, noise reduction, 6-band parametric EQ, vocal compression, and broadcast loudness mastering to -14 LUFS).

faq.question: Can I complete the DaVinci Resolve modules using the free version, or do I need Resolve Studio?
faq.answer: The free version of DaVinci Resolve is 100% sufficient to complete all primary grading, node-based workflows, scopes analysis, Power Windows, planar tracking, CST Log normalization, and Fairlight audio mixing required for your course deliverables. Studio-only neural features (such as IntelliSearch, CineFocus, or Magic Mask) are covered for industry awareness, with accessible manual equivalents provided for all free version users.

faq.question: What features of Runway are taught in the course?
faq.answer: You will explore Runway's generative video toolset: text-to-video, image-to-video priming, motion brush controls for selective regional movement (e.g. animating water or clouds while keeping subjects stable), camera motion controls (pan, tilt, zoom, truck), shot transformation, and generative object replacement.

faq.question: How is AI voiceover generated, and how do we ensure audio-video synchronization?

faq.question: What visual effects (VFX) and motion tracking skills will I learn?

lessons.lesson_title: Visual Communication, Composition & The Grammar of the Shot
lessons.what_is_taught: The principles of visual grammar in moving images: composition, framing, rule of thirds, leading lines, visual hierarchy, contrast, and visual rhythm. Taxonomy of shot sizes (Extreme Long Shot, Long Shot, Medium Shot, Close Up, Extreme Close Up) and psychological camera angles (eye level, high angle, low angle, Dutch angle, bird's eye). Camera movement dynamics (pan, tilt, dolly, truck, zoom, crane, handheld, steadicam) and their emotional impact on viewer engagement.
subtopics: Compositional geometry: rule of thirds, golden ratio, leading lines, framing within frames, and positive vs negative space in video
Visual hierarchy and eye-trace: controlling audience focal attention across rapid sequence cuts
Shot size spectrum: from Extreme Long Shot (establishing context) to Extreme Close Up (intense emotional intimacy)
Camera angles and psychological dominance: high angle vulnerability, low angle empowerment, and Dutch angle disorientation
Dynamic camera movement: distinguishing physical camera travel (dolly/truck) from optical zoom; handheld urgency vs steadicam elegance
lessons.why_it_matters: A video editor cannot build compelling sequences without understanding the visual language established on set by the cinematographer and director.
lessons.what_learner_does: Examines 10 diverse commercial and film scenes, cataloging every shot size, camera angle, and movement type in a visual analysis spreadsheet.
lessons.expected_outcome: A Shot Grammar Deconstruction Matrix analyzing 10 scenes across framing, camera movement, and psychological intent.
lessons.example: Analyzing how a commercial car ad transitions from a wide landscape crane shot to an ECU of the ignition button to generate visceral excitement.

lessons.lesson_title: Continuity Editing, The 180-Degree Rule & Screen Direction
lessons.what_is_taught: The rules of classical spatial and temporal continuity editing: the 180-degree rule (axis of action), 30-degree rule, match-on-action, eyeline matching, and screen direction consistency. Techniques for breaking the 180-degree line deliberately without disorienting the viewer (cutaways, camera movement over the line, neutral buffer shots). Cutaways, insert shots, and point-of-view (POV) editing.
subtopics: The 180-degree rule: establishing the axis of action, camera placement zones, and maintaining left-to-right eye gaze in dialogue
Techniques for crossing the line safely: tracking shots that pivot over the axis, cutaways to neutral objects, or head-on buffer shots
Match-on-action cutting: hiding cuts inside physical subject movement (door opening, sitting down, punch landing) for invisible edits
Eyeline match and spatial orientation: ensuring two actors looking off-screen appear to be looking directly at each other
Screen direction consistency: maintaining left-to-right travel across cuts in chases, commutes, and athletic sequences
lessons.why_it_matters: Violating continuity rules disorients audiences and destroys narrative immersion, signaling amateur editorial craft to agency clients.
lessons.what_learner_does: Analyzes raw footage containing intentional continuity errors and crosses of the axis; re-edits the sequence to restore spatial coherence.
lessons.expected_outcome: A corrected continuity sequence timeline demonstrating flawless match-on-action and spatial orientation.
lessons.example: Editing a dialogue scene between two seated actors where one take crossed the line, inserting a cutaway to a coffee mug to bridge the axis jump.

lessons.lesson_title: Narrative Architecture, Pacing & Emotional Sequencing
lessons.what_is_taught: Story structure across formats: classic 3-act narrative architecture (Setup, Confrontation, Resolution), documentary storytelling curves, and commercial 15/30-second arc constraints. Hook mechanics, narrative pacing, and emotional rhythm. Editing transitions: J-cuts (audio leads video) and L-cuts (video leads audio), match cuts (graphic and audio match cuts), and music-driven montages.
subtopics: Three-act dramatic structure adapted for commercial timelines: 15s social hook, 30s broadcast spot, and 3-minute brand films
Hook construction: establishing emotional stakes and visual curiosity within the opening 3 seconds
The psychology of pacing: metric montage, rhythmic cutting, tonal editing, and intellectual juxtaposition
J-cuts and L-cuts: eliminating jarring split cuts to create natural, conversational audio-visual flow
Graphic match cuts and audio match cuts: using geometric similarity and sound bridges to transition between disparate environments
Music-led storytelling: cutting on the beat vs cutting against the beat (syncopated editing) to avoid predictable mechanical rhythms
lessons.why_it_matters: Pacing is the soul of editing. Great editors manipulate time and rhythm to elicit specific emotional responses from the audience.
lessons.what_learner_does: Takes a flat 60-second interview and cuts two versions: one fast-paced promotional trailer and one contemplative emotional documentary curve.
lessons.expected_outcome: Two distinctly paced edits of the same raw interview exhibiting mastery over rhythm and emotional curves.
lessons.example: Using an L-cut where an interviewee's laughter continues over a B-roll shot of their family, creating deep emotional warmth.

lessons.lesson_title: Technical Video Standards, Codecs, Aspect Ratios & Editorial Planning
lessons.what_is_taught: The technical foundation of digital video: frame rates (24fps cinema, 25fps PAL, 30fps NTSC, 60fps/120fps high-speed for slow motion), resolutions (1080p Full HD, 4K UHD, 8K), pixel aspect ratios, codecs vs containers (ProRes, DNxHD/HR, H.264, H.265, AV1, MP4, MOV). Aspect ratio delivery standards (16:9 widescreen, 9:16 vertical, 1:1 square, 4:5 social feeds). Basic color science (Rec.709, sRGB, Log color profiles). Editing briefs, storyboards, and footage intake logs.
subtopics: Frame rates and temporal motion blur: 24fps film cadence vs 60fps high frame rate; 180-degree shutter rule implications for editorial speed ramps
Codecs vs containers: understanding intra-frame editing codecs (ProRes, DNxHR) vs inter-frame delivery compression (H.264, HEVC)
Aspect ratio strategy: composing multi-format delivery suites (16:9 desktop/TV, 9:16 mobile vertical reels, 1:1 feed tiles, 4:5 portrait)
Color space awareness: understanding Rec.709 display color vs flat camera Log profiles (Sony S-Log3, Canon C-Log, Apple Log)
Editorial planning: reading director briefs, interpreting client shot lists, and logging footage with standardized file-naming conventions
lessons.why_it_matters: Technical errors at the ingest or sequence setup stage cause irreversible playback lag, dropped frames, blown-out colors, and delivery rejection.

Professional folder and bin taxonomy: standardized folder structures for commercial agency delivery

lessons.what_is_taught: The mechanics of high-speed editing: Source Monitor navigation, setting In and Out points (I and O keys), two-handed keyboard editing using J-K-L shuttle controls (double speed, reverse, frame nudge). Three-point and four-point editing principles: Insert (,) and Overwrite (.) operations. Source track patching and timeline track targeting. Building the assembly cut from selects reels using pancake timeline workflows.
subtopics: J-K-L navigation mastery: scrubbing footage at 1x, 2x, 4x, and frame-by-frame without touching the mouse
Three-point editing: defining two points in source and one on timeline (or vice versa) for mathematical cut placement
Track patching vs track targeting: directing video and audio tracks to precise target layers without overwriting existing clips
Pancake timeline editing: stacking a selects sequence above an active assembly timeline for rapid drag-and-drop rough cuts
Subclips and timeline markers: flagging favorite soundbites and visual moments with colored markers and notes
lessons.why_it_matters: Relying on mouse dragging is 5x slower than keyboard-driven three-point editing, distinguishing amateur hobbyists from professional commercial editors.

lessons.lesson_title: Precision Trimming: Ripple, Rolling, Slip & Slide Tools
lessons.what_is_taught: Advanced timeline trimming mechanics: Selection tool vs Razor tool (and why professional editors avoid the razor). Dynamic trimming: Ripple Edit (B), Rolling Edit (N), Slip Edit (Y), and Slide Edit (U). Trim Mode in the Program Monitor (T key) for dual-roller and single-roller trimming. Eliminating jump cuts and refining conversational rhythm with J-cuts and L-cuts (Alt/Option click audio unlinking).
subtopics: Ripple Edit (B): trimming clip duration while automatically closing or expanding downstream timeline gaps
Rolling Edit (N): adjusting the edit point between two adjacent clips without changing the overall sequence length
Slip Edit (Y): shifting the in/out range of footage inside a clip without changing its position or duration on the timeline
Slide Edit (U): moving a clip earlier or later in time while automatically adjusting the durations of adjacent clips
Dual-monitor Trim Mode: nudging edit points frame-by-frame with real-time visual feedback of both outgoing and incoming frames
Executing seamless J-cuts and L-cuts: extending audio beneath incoming or outgoing B-roll to create natural dialogue pacing
lessons.why_it_matters: Trimming is where the real craft of editing happens. Slipping and rolling allows an editor to perfect the emotional timing of an action without breaking sequence duration.
lessons.what_learner_does: Refines an assembly cut using Ripple, Rolling, Slip, and Slide tools, smoothing out awkward dialogue pauses and timing visual actions to music beats.
lessons.expected_outcome: A polished fine cut with seamless audio-visual transitions and calibrated timing.
lessons.example: Using the Slip tool to shift a skateboarder's landing so the wheel hit occurs exactly on the heavy snare beat of the music track.

Transitions best practices: why cross dissolves and hard cuts dominate professional editing, avoiding tacky wipe effects
Essential Graphics Panel: designing broadcast-quality lower third titles with automated responsive pins that adapt to text length
Audio track layering: assigning A1 for dialogue, A2 for ambient room tone, A3-A4 for sound effects, and A5-A6 for stereo music beds
Audio leveling standards: mastering dialogue peaks (-6 to -12 dB) and music beds (-18 to -24 dB) using the Audio Track Mixer

lessons.lesson_title: Proxy Generation, Performance Optimization & Master Export QC

The Multi-Camera Monitor: real-time playback switching, angle swapping, and recording cuts live during timeline playback

Flattening multi-cam sequences: preparing timelines for color grading, visual effects handoff, and online finishing

lessons.what_learner_does: Ingests a 3-camera 4K podcast interview, synchronizes audio waveforms, cuts the sequence live in the Multi-Camera monitor, and refines reaction cuts.

lessons.lesson_title: Time Remapping, Optical Flow Speed Ramping & Velocity Curves
lessons.what_is_taught: Manipulating time and motion dynamics: clip speed/duration vs timeline Time Remapping. Setting time remap keyframes on clip headers, expanding keyframe rubber bands, and sculpting smooth velocity transition curves. Time interpolation algorithms: Frame Sampling, Frame Blending, and Optical Flow (generating synthetic intermediate frames for smooth extreme slow motion). Speed ramping in commercial sports, music video, and product action sequences.
subtopics: Time Remapping interface: accessing time remap controls on timeline track headers and expanding velocity curves
Sculpting bezier speed ramps: creating gradual acceleration and deceleration ramps rather than abrupt speed changes
Optical Flow frame interpolation: understanding motion vector calculations and repairing optical flow warping artifacts
Conforming high frame rate footage: interpreting 60fps/120fps clips to 24fps timelines for native cinematic slow motion
Audio speed pitch shifting: locking audio pitch during speed changes or replacing speed-ramped audio with bespoke sound effects
lessons.why_it_matters: Speed ramps are essential in modern commercial, automotive, and athletic advertising; clunky linear speed changes look amateur.
lessons.what_learner_does: Takes high-speed 120fps athletic footage, applies multi-point speed ramps from normal speed to 10% slow motion and back, using optical flow interpolation.
lessons.expected_outcome: A seamless 30-second commercial action sequence featuring fluid, curve-sculpted speed ramps.
lessons.example: Ramping a basketball player's drive at 200% speed, slowing down to 15% speed at the apex of the dunk, and ramping back to 100% on the rim grab.

Using the Text panel to search spoken dialogue, identify speaker names, and filter out filler words (ums, uhs) and silent pauses. The Paper Edit workflow: highlighting words or sentences directly inside the transcript to instantly insert or assemble corresponding video clips onto the active timeline. Generating and styling automated open and closed captions.

Paper Edit in practice: building a rough cut from an hour-long documentary interview by simply reading and highlighting the transcript
One-click pause and filler word elimination: configuring minimum pause durations (e.g. 0.5s) and bulk deleting timeline gaps
Automated subtitle generation: converting timeline dialogue to synchronized subtitle tracks with custom line-length limits
Styling social captions: applying custom typography, background banners, text drop shadows, and converting subtitles to Essential Graphics
lessons.why_it_matters: Paper Edit and text-based trimming reduce the rough cut assembly phase of interviews and documentaries by up to 70%, dramatically increasing agency profitability.
lessons.what_learner_does: Transcribes an unedited 20-minute interview, removes 30 filler word pauses using bulk deletion, and constructs a 2-minute narrative cut using Paper Edit text selection.
lessons.expected_outcome: A tightly cut 2-minute dialogue edit constructed entirely through transcript-based text editing, complete with synchronized captions.

lessons.lesson_title: Mask Tracking, Lumetri Color Basics, Audio Submixes & Dynamic Link
lessons.what_is_taught: Advanced timeline polishing techniques: creating bezier shape masks on video effects and opacity, configuring mask feathering and expansion, and running the automatic Mask Path tracker. Introduction to Lumetri Color: reading basic waveform scopes, adjusting white balance, exposure, contrast, and applying technical camera LUTs. Professional audio mixing in Premiere: Audio Track Mixer, creating audio submixes (Dialogue, Music, SFX), applying compression and parametric EQ. Establishing Dynamic Link to Adobe After Effects.
subtopics: Mask creation and tracking: applying blurred vignette masks, tracking faces for spot exposure bumps, and isolating moving logos
Lumetri Color fundamentals: reading the Lumetri Waveform to prevent highlight clipping (100 IRE) and shadow crushing (0 IRE)
Applying technical conversion LUTs: transforming camera Log footage into Rec.709 inside Premiere's Basic Correction tab
Audio Submix architecture: routing individual dialogue tracks to a Dialogue Submix bus for unified compression and master leveling
Essential Sound auto-ducking: automatically lowering background music volume whenever dialogue is detected on vocal tracks
Dynamic Link to After Effects: sending a Premiere timeline clip directly to an After Effects comp for motion graphics without intermediate rendering
lessons.why_it_matters: Commercial editors must deliver polished cuts with balanced audio, correct exposure, and integrated graphics before presenting cuts to executive clients.
lessons.what_learner_does: Applies tracked masks to brighten an actor's face, balances exposure with Lumetri, sets up an audio submix with auto-ducking, and sends a title clip to AE via Dynamic Link.
lessons.expected_outcome: A polished commercial scene featuring tracked effect masks, balanced Lumetri exposure, auto-ducked audio submixes, and Dynamic Link integration.

lessons.lesson_title: The Psychology of Retention, Viral Hooks & Pattern Interrupts
lessons.what_is_taught: Audience retention psychology on algorithmic platforms (YouTube, Instagram, TikTok, Meta Ads): analyzing retention graphs, drop-off curves, and completion rates. Hook engineering: the first 3 seconds rule (visual contrast, auditory interrupt, psychological tension). Pacing rhythms and pattern interrupts: scale punch-ins (100% to 115% cuts on key phrases), quick zoom-ins, directional pans, sound hits (whoosh, risers, thuds, vinyl stops), and onscreen text emphasis to reset viewer dopamine and sustain engagement.
subtopics: Audience retention analytics: diagnosing why 50% of viewers drop off before second 5 and structuring edits to push 70%+ completion
The Anatomy of a Viral Hook: visual spectacle hooks, contradictory statement hooks, and open-loop curiosity questions
Pattern interrupts: executing subtle 10-15% jump punch-ins on punchlines to maintain visual novelty without jarring the viewer
B-roll layering for cognitive clarity: cutting to relevant visual demonstrations before the speaker finishes explaining the concept
Avoidance of visual fatigue: balancing fast-paced editing with breathing room moments so audiences are not overwhelmed
lessons.why_it_matters: Clients do not pay for videos that get scrolled past; retention-driven editing directly dictates organic reach and paid ad conversion rates.
lessons.what_learner_does: Analyzes a raw talking-head video with a steep drop-off curve, scripts and edits 3 distinct opening hooks, and introduces pattern interrupts throughout.
lessons.expected_outcome: A high-retention 60-second video cut featuring 3 distinct hook variations ready for A/B testing.
lessons.example: Editing a financial education video where the opening 3 seconds begins with a dramatic sound drop and a cash register punch-in, arresting scroll fatigue.

lessons.lesson_title: Kinetic Social Captioning, Emphasis Graphics & Dynamic Sound Design

Designing onscreen motion callouts: graphic arrows, highlighted document snippets, lower third badges, and product price tags. Commercial sound design: layering atmospheric ambient beds, whooshes on camera transitions, risers before key moments, impact hits on text reveals, and UI clicks.

Graphic callouts and screen highlighting: animating spotlight masks over documents and web screenshots to guide viewer eyes
The sonic layer of retention editing: why sound design accounts for 60% of perceived production value in short-form video
Layering Foley and impact SFX: combining a low sub-drop with a high whoosh and a paper rustle to create powerful multi-tonal impacts
Music beat synchronization: cutting video action to musical downbeats, snare hits, and cutting audio on dramatic narrative pauses
lessons.why_it_matters: Over 75% of social media video is consumed on mute or with divided attention; bold kinetic captions and rich sound design maximize comprehension and retention.
lessons.what_learner_does: Adds kinetic highlighted captions, 5 custom graphic callouts, and a 12-layer sound design bed to a 60-second product advertisement.
lessons.expected_outcome: A dynamic short-form video with synchronized kinetic subtitles, visual callouts, and commercial sound design.

Master campaign packaging: structuring client delivery folders with clean video versions, subtitled versions, and audio stems

lessons.lesson_title: Human-in-the-Loop Quality Control, Artifact Repair & Credit Management

Enterprise compliance: understanding commercial indemnification in Adobe Firefly, client disclosure obligations, and avoiding copyright infringement

lessons.lesson_title: Composition, Visual Hierarchy & Layout Systems in Motion

Building responsive 8pt layout systems for 1920x1080 (landscape) and 1080x1920 (vertical reels). Layout systems and 8pt design grid architecture adapted to 1920x1080 and 3840x2160 motion graphics canvases

Title-safe and action-safe boundaries (EBU R95 and SMPTE ST 2048) versus modern social media safe zones
Visual hierarchy: controlling viewer eye path using scale contrast, tonal weight, and focal points
Colour theory and brand consistency: establishing motion palettes, tint/shade variations, and contrast ratios

lessons.lesson_title: Typography for Video & Motion Principles

Kerning, tracking, line length, and leading for fast video readability. Translating static typographic layouts into dynamic time-based choreography with predictable readability dwell times.

Motion principles in design: understanding timing and spacing to give graphical weight to UI and typographic elements

Squash and stretch awareness: planning deformable graphics versus rigid geometric shapes
Easing and motion curves: conceptualizing acceleration, deceleration, and velocity profiles before entering software

lessons.lesson_title: Asset Engineering: Illustrator Layer Separation & Photoshop Cutouts

Illustrator layer separation protocol: top-level layers vs sublayers, naming standards, and grouping rules
Vector cleanup: flattening appearances, expanding strokes, releasing clipping masks, and anchor point alignment
Photoshop cutouts and mask preparation: precision Pen Tool paths, Refine Edge hair masking, and clean alpha channels
Parallax assets preparation: reconstructing plates with Generative Fill and slicing depth planes for 2.5D environments
lessons.why_it_matters: Improperly layered or named files waste hours of studio time and break when imported into After Effects.
lessons.what_learner_does: Takes a complex brand illustration, executes Illustrator layer separation across 15+ named layers, produces Photoshop cutouts with mask preparation, and slices parallax assets.
lessons.expected_outcome: A production-ready Illustrator file and Photoshop multi-layer PSD completely prepared for direct After Effects animation.

Simulating organic physical properties: inertia, mass, gravity, rebound, and overshoot. Enabling and configuring motion blur: shutter angle, samples per frame, and GPU acceleration for hyper-fluid motion physics.

lessons.what_is_taught: Inception phase of an enterprise commercial production: client brief interpretation, decoding commercial objectives, target audience demographics, and calls to action (CTA). Formulating creative strategy and pitch deck. Asset inventory and budget planning: organizing raw footage, graphics, and music licenses. Establishing production schedules, team roles, and creative milestones. Developing detailed visual storyboards and seeking storyboard approval. Building a timed animatic with scratch voiceover and temporary music to lock editorial pacing and sequence duration before executing final motion graphics and VFX.
subtopics: Client brief interpretation: extracting core value propositions, campaign tone, and mandatory brand guidelines
Creative strategy and story concept: developing high-impact narrative hooks and persuasive commercial structures
Production schedule and milestones: establishing deadlines for script lock, animatic sign-off, rough cut, and picture lock
Asset inventory and licensing: cataloging live footage, stock clips, brand vector kits, and audio stems
Storyboard approval: presenting style frames, camera annotations, and visual concepts to simulated client boards
Animatic development: constructing a timed 2D animatic to lock pacing, voiceover cadence, and shot transitions
lessons.why_it_matters: Professional commercial agencies never begin full animation or editing without an approved animatic; locking pacing early prevents costly rebuilds during post-production.
lessons.what_learner_does: Interprets a simulated enterprise brief, writes the creative treatment, builds an approved storyboard, and delivers a timed animatic with scratch audio.
lessons.expected_outcome: An approved pre-production package including creative treatment, asset inventory, schedule, and locked animatic.
lessons.example: Creating an animatic for a sustainable electric vehicle commercial locking scene durations at 4s, 3s, 5s, and 3s before filming or animating.

lessons.lesson_title: Master Editing, Brand Motion, VFX & AI Integration
lessons.what_is_taught: Executing production and post-production phases: assembling the master timeline in Premiere Pro. Cutting traditional footage with rhythmic precision, applying J/L cuts, and maintaining narrative continuity. Designing brand motion graphics in After Effects: kinetic title sequences, animated lower thirds, and animated logo stings. Executing VFX integration: planar tracking, screen replacement, and subject rotoscoping. Incorporating AI-generated footage where justified (surreal environments, macro product perspectives, or background extensions) and compositing with matched lighting, shadows, and camera grain.
subtopics: Master timeline editing: cutting live-action footage with narrative rhythm and high-retention pacing
Brand motion design: crafting custom animated typography, title cards, and logo stings in After Effects
VFX integration: executing screen replacements, object cleanup, and multi-plane 2.5D camera moves
Justified AI-generated footage integration: generating and compositing complex visual assets with matching lighting and grain
Multi-layer compositing: assembling complex visual stacks with foreground subjects, background plates, and motion graphics
Rough cut assembly: merging all visual disciplines into a cohesive 45–60 second picture-locked timeline
lessons.why_it_matters: Synthesizing editing, motion design, VFX, and AI into a singular, polished timeline is the ultimate demonstration of an industry-ready video professional.
lessons.what_learner_does: Edits the 45–60s master commercial, builds custom motion graphics, executes VFX screen replacements, and composites AI-generated environmental plates.
lessons.expected_outcome: A picture-locked 45–60 second commercial master integrating live footage, motion graphics, VFX, and justified AI assets.
lessons.example: Editing an athletic shoe commercial where live footage of a runner seamlessly transitions into an AI-generated digital terrain with glowing motion graphics.

lessons.lesson_title: Colour Grading, Fairlight Audio Mix, Client Feedback & Delivery QA
lessons.what_is_taught: Finishing, audio post-production, and client revision management: executing professional node-based colour grading in DaVinci Resolve. Harmonizing disparate cameras and AI clips to a unified cinematic look with calibrated skin tones and legal scopes. Sound editing and mixing in Fairlight: dialogue restoration, sound-effect layering, sidechain ducking, and loudness normalization to -14 LUFS. Managing client feedback: decoding subjective client notes, conducting revision simulation, and managing versioning. Final delivery QA: inspecting audio sync, flash frames, color banding, and metadata compliance.
subtopics: Cinematic colour grading in DaVinci Resolve: CST normalization, shot matching, and creative look styling
Fairlight sound mixing: dialogue cleanup, Foley sound design, dynamic ducking, and -14 LUFS mastering
Client feedback management: translating client revision requests into actionable technical tasks
Revision simulation: executing client-requested adjustments (pacing tweaks, color trim, graphic text updates)
Delivery QA checklist: conducting exhaustive quality control for audio sync, illegal broadcast colors, and compression artifacts
Master packaging: preparing final ProRes masters, client review files, and project archival handoffs
lessons.why_it_matters: Mastery over client revisions, sound mixing, and color grading separates entry-level editors from trusted post-production supervisors.
lessons.what_learner_does: Grades the commercial in Resolve, mixes audio to -14 LUFS in Fairlight, executes simulated client revisions, and runs a comprehensive delivery QA.
lessons.expected_outcome: A broadcast-ready, fully graded, sound-mixed 45–60 second commercial master passing all delivery QA standards.
lessons.example: Grading a commercial to a warm filmic look, ducking energetic music under voiceover, and adjusting graphic text based on client feedback.

lessons.lesson_title: Duration Cutdowns: 60s, 30s & 15s Commercial Restructuring
lessons.what_is_taught: The mechanics of commercial cutdowns: restructuring a 60-second master edit into an impactful 30-second version and a hyper-condensed 15-second cutdown. Preserving the core narrative hook, emotional progression, and call to action (CTA) under severe time constraints. Re-timing voiceovers, re-cutting music beds with seamless audio splices, and condensing motion graphic transitions. Maintaining story coherence and message clarity without feeling rushed or truncated.
subtopics: Master edit deconstruction: identifying non-essential beats and redundant coverage
Structuring the 30-second cut: streamlining narrative progression while retaining emotional resonance
The 15-second cutdown formula: instant hook (0-3s), problem/solution (3-10s), and punchy CTA (10-15s)
Audio re-timing: cutting music stems on bar beats and tightening voiceover spacing
Motion graphics re-scaling: accelerating lower third dwell times and animating concise logo stings
Duration quality control: ensuring exact frame-accurate runtime compliance (e.g. exactly 15;00 frames for broadcast/social)
lessons.why_it_matters: Brands allocate the majority of digital ad spend to 15s and 30s cutdowns; editors who can distill 60s stories into high-converting short formats are indispensable.
lessons.what_learner_does: Takes the 60s capstone master commercial and edits both a 30-second version and a 15-second cutdown with restructured audio and graphics.
lessons.expected_outcome: Two cohesive, frame-accurate commercial cutdown edits (30s and 15s) with seamless music edits and locked CTA timing.
lessons.example: Condensing a 60-second car commercial into a 15-second high-octane cutdown focusing solely on vehicle acceleration and weekend sale pricing.

lessons.lesson_title: Aspect Ratio Reformatting: Vertical 9:16, Square & Safe Zones
lessons.what_is_taught: Cross-platform aspect ratio conversion: transforming 16:9 landscape master edits into 9:16 vertical versions (TikTok, Instagram Reels, YouTube Shorts) and 1:1 square versions. Dynamic framing adjustments: utilizing Premiere's Auto-Reframe with custom keyframing to track moving subjects. Designing multi-stack split-screens for vertical viewing. Respecting social media UI overlay zones: avoiding native platform buttons, like icons, caption bars, and profile links. Verifying subtitle-safe areas and CTA/safe zones. Standardizing version naming, export profiles, colour consistency, and asset packaging.
subtopics: Aspect ratio geometry: mathematical scaling and re-centering between 16:9, 9:16, and 1:1 canvases
Framing adjustments: tracking moving actors and products across vertical viewports with manual keyframing
Multi-stack and split-screen layouts: positioning B-roll above dialogue for engaging vertical storytelling
Subtitle-safe areas and CTA/safe zones: overlaying TikTok/Reels UI templates to protect text and logos
Export profiles and render optimization: configuring bitrates and NCLC color tags for flawless mobile playback
Version naming and asset packaging: building clean delivery folders (CLIENT_PROJECT_DELIVERY_V01) with master and cutdown assets
lessons.why_it_matters: Over 80% of digital video consumption occurs vertically on mobile devices; text or logos obscured by TikTok or Instagram buttons results in rejected ad campaigns.

lessons.example: Re-framing a horizontal interview into a 9:16 vertical reel where subtitles and logo remain perfectly centered within TikTok's active safe zone.

lessons.what_is_taught: Engineering a world-class 60–90-second motion graphics and video editing showreel. Showcasing versatile disciplines: commercial editing, kinetic typography, 3D tracking, visual effects, color grading, and hybrid AI production. Eliminating filler, student-exercise aesthetics, and un-cleared assets.
subtopics: Portfolio strategy: positioning your reel for commercial agencies vs broadcast networks vs high-ticket freelance
